coverage_notes: Apache License 2.0 section 3’s patent grant also covers making, having made, offering to sell, importing, and otherwise transferring the Work. Those acts have no faithful representation in the fixed activity vocabulary; the existing patent-use and patent-sale anchors cover only the expressible aspects.

Apache License 2.0 section 5’s default treatment of intentionally submitted Contributions, including the exception for an explicit contrary statement and the carveout for separate license agreements, concerns submission and the resulting licensing treatment. Submit is not an allowed activity, and no available activity faithfully represents that rule.

paragraph_audit.reason: The cited anchors cover the expressible patent-use and sale grants and the litigation-triggered termination. The remaining patent-grant acts—making, having made, offering to sell, importing, and otherwise transferring—do not fit any allowed activity.

Section 5 governs intentionally submitting a Contribution and its default licensing treatment, subject to an explicit contrary statement and any separate license agreement. The submission action and resulting default cannot be faithfully represented by an allowed activity.
